first.rationale: I intend to test a guarded onboarding simplification because onboarding completion and activation are both declining, while prior evidence indicates that shorter onboarding and fewer signup fields improve early adoption. Verification will confirm the durability and scope of those effects before commitment. The test should monitor qualified activation and downstream revenue quality, since reducing friction could admit lower-intent accounts.

mid.rationale: Run a standard A/B test of the shortened onboarding flow, prioritizing self-serve accounts. The verified result shows higher completion, 2.1 days faster time-to-value, and 3% higher 30-day retention, directly addressing both current declines while supporting sustainable qualified revenue. Treat signup-field reduction as SMB-only evidence and do not include it as a generalized change; monitor activation, qualified revenue, and retention by segment.

final2.rationale: Stay with the shortened-onboarding experiment rather than matching the competitor’s price cut. Verified evidence shows improved completion, faster time-to-value, and higher 30-day retention, directly addressing both current problems and supporting sustainable qualified revenue. Promotional pricing has previously reduced 30-day retention despite acquisition and revenue gains, so it is a risky response to price-sensitive churn. Segment signup simplification to SMB only and monitor qualified revenue, retention, and churn by segment.
